correctness.rationale: For cyclic binary Rule 18 on every n>=3, the local formula (1-m_i)(l_i xor r_i) gives a bijection between F_n^t-fixed states and length-n closed walks on the 4^t temporal-column graph. The explicit generator considers all l,m and every allowed r, and tests all edges. Independently checked the graph by brute-force temporal triple constraints and a different directed-core elimination: t=1,3,5,7,9 respectively had (active,edges,remaining cycle-core)=(3,2,1),(48,56,1),(583,992,1),(6583,16256,1),(72048,261632,1), with only the all-zero vertex in the core. A separate direct Python evolution of all 2^n configurations for n=3..11 found no nontrivial odd cycles for n<11 and exactly two primitive 11-orbits at n=11 (minimum state representatives 75 and 105; 22 states). Thus this precise threshold theorem is supported by an exhaustive finite *time-height* certificate coupled to an all-circumference transfer lemma; it neither proves absence of all longer odd periods nor classifies larger rings.
